noncalcareous and calcareous sandstone with minor sandy and cherty limestone; Pseudoschwagerina Schwagerina fusulinids; OQUIRRH GROUP in SO. CURLEW VALLEY Miller and Langrock (1997) divided Oquirrh rocks in the Hansel Mountains on the southeast edge at Curlew Valley into three informal members:

chert & sandstone minor limestone; interbedded sandstone & limestone 2100 feet; limestone, sandstone & minor chert 1300 feet; interbedded sandstone & limetsone 1200 feet; 3) VARIABLE LITHOLOGY MEMBER (Permian): platy limestone calcarenite, calcareous sandstone, and siltstone; about 6000 feet thick.; 2) SANDSTONE MEMBER: very fine-grained calcareous sandstone and orthoquartzites commonly cross-bedded; Permian fusulinids rare; more than 9,500 feet thick; 1) LAMINATED LIMESTONE MEMBER (Upper Pennsylvanian): silty and sandy calcarenite, and very fine-grained quartz sandstone; wavy laminations caused by bioturbation; at least 2000 feet thick
